request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Hospital Course Summary:

Patient Name: [Name]

Admission Date: 20 March 2020

Discharge Date: [Date]
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Significant Past Medical History:
- Ischaemic myocardiopathy with left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation in 2012
- Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
- Recurrent anaemia due to gastrointestinal bleeding
- Arteriovenous malformations

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for blood transfusion due to ongoing gastrointestinal bleeding. The patient was diagnosed with COVID-19 during hospitalization. The patient’s INR was found to be high on admission and was treated with parenteral heparin. Three units of red blood cells were transfused, which restored haemoglobin to normal levels. The melaena was controlled with precise control of anti-Xa under heparin infusion, and VKA was reintroduced after the resolution of melaena. The patient was managed for respiratory issues during hospitalization and was discharged with regular teleconsultations to monitor INR and respiratory parameters.

Hospital Course Details:
- Admission date: 20 March 2020
- Reason for admission: Gastrointestinal bleeding
- COVID-19 status: Positive test, asymptomatic
- Management:
  - Parenteral heparin to treat high INR
  - Blood transfusion to restore haemoglobin levels
  - Monitoring respiratory parameters
  - Regular teleconsultations for INR monitoring and management
- Discharge date: [Date]

Summary:
The patient with a history of ischaemic myocardiopathy and LVAD implantation was admitted for gastrointestinal bleeding and was diagnosed with COVID-19 during hospitalization. The patient’s high INR was treated with parenteral heparin, and after a blood transfusion and resolution of melaena, VKA was reintroduced. The patient was managed for respiratory issues and was discharged with regular teleconsultations for continued monitoring of INR and respiratory parameters.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The admission was for blood transfusion because of ongoing gastrointestinal bleeding (melaena) in a patient with arteriovenous malformations and recurrent anaemia. COVID-19 was an incidental, asymptomatic finding during the stay, so it is not the principal diagnosis.

The candidate categories are:
- K92 (melaena, K92.1), which is the sign-level code.
- K31 (angiodysplasia of the stomach and duodenum, K31.8).
- K55 (vascular disorders of the intestine, with angiodysplasia of the colon at K55.2).
- D50 (iron deficiency anaemia secondary to blood loss).
- D62 (acute posthaemorrhagic anaemia).

The site of the AVMs is not stated, which makes K55 or K31 hard to justify. Melaena with an unspecified source codes to K92.1, and the bleeding was the reason for admission and what was treated. The anticoagulation involved a high INR with bleeding, which would add a drug-adverse-effect code (D68.3) as a secondary diagnosis, though that is not the principal one.

I chose K92 because the bleeding with melaena was the condition treated and no bleeding site was specified.

CODE: K92
